newsitem.title: USA: Nautilus gets ok for Gulf gas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Nautilus gets ok for Gulf gas pipeline.

text.p: Nautilus Pipeline Co. LLC said Wednesday it has has received regulatory approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to build a $121 million natural gas pipeline in the central Gulf of Mexico.
Nautilus is owned by affiliates of Shell Oil Co., which has a 50 percent stake, Leviathan Gas Pipeline Partners LP, with a 25.67 percent interest and Marathon Oil Co., with a 24.33 percent stake.
The company said construction of the 101-mile, 30-inch pipeline is expected to begin in early April and should be completed by November.

The pipeline, with a capacity of 600 million cubic feet of gas per day, will connect with the Manta Ray Offshore Gathering System and extend onshore to Exxon Corp.'s Garden City gas plant in southern Louisiana for redelivery to multiple onshore transmission lines.
Marathon will oversee construction of the pipeline and onshore facilities.
